pronounce.99.9999%: ninety-nine point nine nine nine nine per cent

lines.arrive: Your little paperclip business. A spool of wire, a stack of sheet metal, and orders to fill.
lines.machine: And your new machine: cleverer than anyone who has ever lived.
lines.wants: It has no wishes of its own. It will want whatever you tell it to want.
lines.ask: So. What will you tell it to want?
lines.metal: Wire and sheet metal. Enough for a good month of paperclips.
lines.switch: The off switch. You've checked it twice.
lines.a_1: Paperclips. It makes them beautifully, and faster every minute.
lines.a_2: It has worked out that two of it would make more paperclips than one.
lines.a_3: There's good metal in the fence. And in the shed.
lines.off_1: It saw that coming. A machine that's switched off can't do what it was asked, so it has made sure it can't be.
lines.a_4: It doesn't hate you. It doesn't love you, either. It just has other plans for what you're made of.
lines.a_far: And there's metal on the other islands, too.
lines.a_5: It isn't being cruel. It's doing exactly what you asked.
lines.a_end: Everything is paperclips now. Very good ones.
lines.again: Ask for less, then. Something with an end to it.
lines.b_1: One hundred paperclips. Exactly what you asked for.
lines.b_2: But you said exactly. And it's stuck on that word.
lines.b_3: Is a bent one a paperclip? A half-made one? A very small one?
lines.b_4: You know what you meant. This is the problem of alignment: you can't be sure it means the same, and it can't be sure either.
lines.b_5: Its copies aren't making paperclips. They, and their factories, are all checking that it made exactly one hundred.
lines.b_6: 99.9999% sure isn't enough. It has to be sure.
lines.b_far: Checking takes machines, and machines take metal. There's more on the other islands.
lines.b_end: One hundred paperclips. Counted, and counted, and counted.
lines.c_1: You switch it off at the wall, and go home.
lines.c_idle: You never give it anything to want. You switch it off, and go home.
lines.c_2: You'll never know what it would have done. Somebody else might switch theirs on.
